contract: Surface temperature = meanCelsius + beltAmplitudeCelsius * cos(2 pi z / beltPeriodBlocks) + noiseAmplitudeCelsius * (broad + detailWeight * detail) / (1 + detailWeight), with broad noise at scaleBlocks and detail at scaleBlocks * detailScaleFraction, both on domain-warped coordinates that ClimateMap shares. A belt period of 0 disables the belt.

Background moisture = 0.5 + 0.5 * contrast(T) * (broad + detailWeight * detail) / (1 + detailWeight) + beltAmplitude * cos(2 pi (x + beltOffsetBlocks) / beltPeriodBlocks) + shift(T), clamped to 0..1, on the same warped coordinates, broad at broadBlocks and detail at detailBlocks, before upwind forcing (riven-climate-forcing.json). The moisture belt runs east-west, across the temperature belt, so every climate band spans dry to wet; a belt period of 0 disables it.

Temperature profile (climate-v4): shift(T) and contrast(T) are linear between temperatureProfile stops {celsius, shift, contrast} on the column's surface temperature (before province offsets) and held beyond the ends; contrast defaults to 1 and none means 0 and 1. Dry subtropics with sharper contrast in the warm band put deserts and rainforests side by side, as a mean shift alone cannot: over six seeds (8 km, terrain-v107) hot desert rose from 4.2% to 7.5% of land, dry from 18.6% to 26.2%, and rainforest from 5.2% to 6.6% while wet land stayed at 28%. A shift of -0.22 without contrast reached 7% desert but cut rainforest to 3%.
Temperature reads no altitude, plates, water or biome; later layers consume it.

Lapse rate (climate-v5): at intent, after the province offsets, a land column cools by celsiusPerBlock for every block its coarse base height (BaseTerrainMap, before landforms and fine detail) stands above the sea beyond startAboveSeaBlocks, and is reclassified; the treeline reads the climate before this cooling, since it has its own height rule. Starting above most land keeps lowland climate as tuned and makes high ground cold: over six seeds (8 km, terrain-v108) frozen land rose from 14.3% to 19.7% and north-south position's correlation with land temperature fell from 0.978 to 0.927, while hot desert went from 7.5% to 6.6% and rainforest from 6.6% to 5.6%.

Tuned for 8 km worlds (32 km maximum): a 16 km belt with the origin on the mean gives every 8 km world half a cycle; belts and wavelengths scale with the layout, so a 32 km world (layout scale 4) keeps the same half cycle; target blend about 20% cold (FROZEN), 60% temperate (COOL, MILD, WARM), 20% hot (HOT). Moisture (climate-v3): features at 2,000 and 800 blocks give an 8 km world several wet and dry lobes, and the belt (wet west, dry east, half a cycle per 8 km world) keeps them from lining up with the temperature bands; over six seeds dry land (riven-biomes.json cores) is 16-31% and forest climates 50-75%.
